feedback.problem: Calculate the points where the hyperbola $5{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}=20$ intersects the line $y=-\sqrt{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=-\sqrt{2},$ we substitute $y=-\sqrt{2}$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2} & =20 \\ 5(-\sqrt{2})^{2}-4{x}^{2} & =20 \\ 5(2)-4{x}^{2} & =20 \\ 10-4{x}^{2} & =20 \\ -4{x}^{2} & =10 \\ {x}^{2} & =-\frac{10}{4} \\ {x}^{2} & =-\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We cannot take the square root of a negative number. Therefore, the equation has no real solutions. 
So, the hyperbola does not intersect the horizontal line $y=-\sqrt{2}.$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: There are no points of intersection
